record.paper_title: Open Problems in Geometric Methods for Instance-Based Learning
record.original_question: How should a reduced training set be selected so that it still represents the different classes well enough for effective instance-based classification?

evidence.quote: How should the reduced training set be selected to represent the different classes?

artifact.status_search_result: The question of how to optimally select a reduced training set for instance-based (nearest-neighbor) classification while preserving class representation is a long-standing open research direction. Many heuristic methods exist (CNN, ENN, IB2/IB3, DROP, prototype generation, coresets for $k$-NN), but no canonical optimal solution with full theoretical guarantees is generally accepted; the problem remains an active area without a definitive resolution.

status_evidence.title: Survey of Instance Selection for Instance-Based Learning
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys numerous heuristic instance selection algorithms and notes that no single method dominates across datasets.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of optimal training set reduction for instance-based learning remains unresolved with competing heuristics.

status_evidence.title: Coresets for k-NN classification
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work develops coreset constructions with approximation guarantees for nearest-neighbor classifiers, indicating ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical guarantees for reduced sets are still being actively developed.
